items.summary: Nvidia has opened an independent investigation after reports that its CEO Jensen Huang had a relationship with Alice Huang, whom US intelligence officials believe was spying for China. The company said the board found no reason to think Nvidia secrets or national security were compromised and added that Huang remains committed to leading it. Separately, Huang admitted being unfaithful to his wife, apologised for hurting her and their children, and took full responsibility. He said he supports the investigation and will cooperate fully. Trump said he had not spoken to Huang since news emerged but called him an honourable guy.
items.title: Nvidia Opens Probe Into CEO's Alleged Ties To Chinese Spy

items.summary: On Sunday, US President Donald Trump called Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang an honorable person and praised his contributions to the United States. However, when asked about allegations that Huang had a relationship with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to Beijing, Trump said he had not spoken to Huang about it. Nvidia separately reported it was investigating whether Huang faced a foreign intelligence effort.
items.title: Trump Calls Huang Honorable, Denies Discussing Allegations

items.summary: On November 9, Nvidia announced it was opening an investigation into reports that CEO Jensen Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. The announcement followed Huang’s admission to the board that he had been intimate with Alice Huang, whom US intelligence determined was feeding information directly to Beijing. In a message to the company, Huang apologized and said there was no excuse for what he did.
items.title: Nvidia Opens Probe Into Jensen Huang’s Affair With Chinese Spy

items.summary: Nvidia's board announced an investigation into reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort, citing The New York Times. Huang acknowledged being intimate with Alice Huang, whom US intelligence said fed information to Beijing; he apologized and said his actions hurt his wife and children. Nvidia stated it has no reason to believe national security or its secrets were compromised, while Huang committed to cooperating.
items.title: Nvidia Investigates Reports of Foreign Intelligence Targeting Jensen Huang

items.summary: The RBI offered a hedging facility for the $133 billion raised under its special foreign-currency-deposit window, but it does not cover interest on FCNR(B) deposits. Banks must buy dollars forward themselves and many have no strategy yet, so they keep returning to the market as liabilities accrue. Some may hedge once the rupee rises; others hedged after costs fell within internal thresholds.
items.title: RBI's FCNR(B) window leaves banks exposed to dollar interest costs

items.summary: Congress Rajya Sabha MP Jairam Ramesh on Sunday criticised Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his "Dimagi Naxals" remarks, calling them a brazen assault and accusing him of using Diwali to target political rivals. In an X post, Ramesh said Modi hurled invectives during his Bastar visit and cited earlier comments labelling caste-census protesters as "urban naxals" on April 28, 2024, before a census was announced for Census 2027, plus Sept 2020 remarks about farm-law opponents. Ramesh said the PM is distraught, disturbed and desperate, adding Jhola-picking-up time is fast approaching.
items.title: Congress MP Jairam Ramesh calls Modi's 'Dimagi Naxals' remark a brazen assault

items.summary: Family members of Adam Mark Perrim, accused of the domestic violence murder of Danielle Madgwick in south-western New South Wales on 19 September, have been charged with being accessories after the fact to murder. The trio—Perrim's brother Bailey Perrim, his father George Maxwell Richard Perrim, and his mother Julie Ann Collins—are alleged to have known Madgwick. They were refused bail at a committal hearing.
items.title: Wagga Wagga Family Members Charged as Accessories After Domestic Violence Murder

items.summary: The New Zealand dollar rose after too-close weekend elections left the government weakened, though vote counting continues until November 27. The US dollar index held steady at 102.20 as October jobs growth accelerated and unemployment fell. Futures imply around 79% odds of a December rate hike versus 71% earlier. Fed officials cited resilient growth but high inflation.
items.title: New Zealand and US Currencies Firm on Jobs Data and Election Uncertainty

items.summary: Wall Street Journal reporter Evan Gershkovich became the first U.S. journalist arrested for espionage in Russia since the Cold War when FSB agents detained him in Yekaterinburg on March 29, 2023. He was sentenced to 16 years before being freed in an August 2024 prisoner swap. Gershkovich, the Journal and the U.S. government deny he was a spy. Speaking from Canada about his new book, he discusses prison life and Putin's Russia.
items.title: Gershkovich Reflects on Arrest, Prison and Freedom in New Book

items.summary: Raheim Brown Jr hit a winning three-pointer on his NBL debut for the Adelaide 36ers, who beat Illawarra by 28 points at an Entertainment Centre crowd of over 10,000. The 16-year-old had been on court just 73 seconds when he shot. He is now the youngest debutant in club history and previously became the youngest player signed by a club in 44 years.
items.title: Young Adelaide debutant scores buzzer-beater in sellout arena

items.summary: Authorities in Indonesia have named the two survivors of a fatal helicopter crash as investigations continue into its cause. Australian Michael Betteridge and New Zealander Hugh Page survived when their aircraft nosedived into a river while collecting water to fight fires on Borneo, killing navigator Yayan Supyansuri. The incident follows another crew death in November.
items.title: Survivors of Indonesian helicopter crash named after fatal water-bombing accident

items.summary: Paris' Musée d'Orsay opened a permanent room displaying paintings suspected of being looted by Nazis during the Second World War, whose true owners have never been found. Ines Rotermund-Reynard, the museum's head provenance researcher, leads efforts to confirm each work's ownership history and locate rightful heirs or descendants. The exhibit reflects France's ongoing mission to reopen sealed wartime archives and advance restitution; French museums hold about 2,000 likely Nazi-looted works in temporary custody. Over the last three decades, France has returned 16 paintings to families, with pace increasing even roughly 80 years after the war.
items.title: Orsay Opens Room Tracing Nazi-Looted Art

items.summary: On 8th November 2026, the author tested building a SQLite extension that adds a parse_number() function to convert strings like -$1,234.56 or '12.5%' into numeric values. Using Claude Opus 5.5, they compared C and Rust versions: the Rust extensions measured at 321 KB (Rusqlite) and 298 KB (sqlite-loadable-rs), while the C extension was 14 KB. Despite its smaller size, the Rust version proved faster because it used strtod twice as fast.
items.title: Author benchmarks SQLite parse_number in C and Rust

items.summary: The Indian passport rose one place on the October 2026 Henley Passport Index, but its access fell from 57 to 55 destinations. A Gulf News breakdown counted only about 25 true visa-free entries. The article focuses on how long each country permits a stay: Malaysia allows 30 days until 31 December 2026; Thailand cut stays from 60 to 30 days from 15 September 2026; Fiji offers up to about 120 days, while Mauritius and Barbados allow 90. Sources disagree on places such as the Maldives, so travellers are advised to check official embassy pages before booking.
items.title: India's passport slips as visa-free stays tighten abroad

items.summary: The article explains that an air purifier's yearly cost includes electricity and replacement filters. Using Eureka Forbes' guide of ₹8 per unit, a 35W machine run for 12 hours daily costs about ₹1,210 annually; at Delhi slab extremes it ranges from about ₹38 to ₹181 monthly. Adding one filter change yearly brings running costs to ₹2,810 low and ₹10,210 high, with a first-year total of roughly ₹18,800 to ₹26,200 once the machine price is included. The figures are illustrations; readers should check their own bills and model-specific filter prices.
items.title: Delhi air purifier running costs range from ₹2,810 to ₹10,210 a year

items.summary: Paraguay's president was removed from office and detained after Ueno, the country's largest digital bank, collapsed amid allegations of insider lending and ties to its longtime ruling party. The app had expanded access in a region where as many as one in four adults lacks a bank account; officials called it 'a kind of tsunami,' leaving half the populace without funds.
items.title: Paraguay's President Removed After Digital Bank Collapse

items.summary: Oil Minister Basim Mohammed Khudair said Iraq is already producing more than 5 million bpd, over half a million above its current OPEC+ requirement of 4.431 million bpd, complicating Baghdad's bid for a larger allocation ahead of the group's 2027 framework. The Oil Ministry reaffirmed the 4.431 million bpd ceiling shortly after. Iraq reported 4.399 million bpd in September to OPEC and shipped about 3.5 million bpd in October, so reaching Khudair's level would require at least 601,000 bpd of unexplained output. The IEA estimated September production at 4.10 million bpd and sustainable capacity at 4.87 million bpd. OPEC assesses compliance using independent estimates rather than Baghdad's own figures, so Khudair's claim is not yet confirmed by the group or third parties. For Charles Kennedy for Oilprice.com.
items.title: Iraq's Higher Output Claim Undermines Its OPEC Quota Request

items.summary: Around 80 world leaders, including Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, are meeting this week in Antalya for the annual UN climate summit, COP31. For the first time, host duties fall to Turkey while Australia leads negotiations. The talks consider a global electrification target of “35 by 35”, raising electricity’s share from just over 20% today toward 35% by 2035. Global clean-energy investment this year reached A$3.2 trillion, twice that spent on fossil fuels. Though consensus-based agreements are often incremental and the US has withdrawn completely, supporters argue COP31 can still deliver real progress amid a heating planet.
items.title: World Leaders Gather at COP31 Climate Summit in Turkey

items.summary: Rest of World reports that AI infrastructure is absorbing memory-chip supply, ending the era of cheap smartphones and pushing up prices globally. Prices of existing models rose about 15% this year, with new launches roughly 25% dearer than last year. The jump varies sharply by region: 21% in India, 19% across Asia-Pacific, 18% in the Middle East and Africa, versus just 5% in the US. Ivan Lam of Counterpoint says Chinese makers have cut entry-level output as chip costs climb. Ramon Llamas of IDC warns the shortage will not ease soon. GSMA's Claire Sibthorpe fears rising handset prices could widen digital inequality by making affordable phones harder to reach.
items.title: AI Chip Demand Drives Record Smartphone Price Jumps in India

items.summary: Mihail Eric, who leads Monaco and teaches Stanford's CS146S course on modern software development, revisited the second run of his class to show how it changed after working alongside his own engineering team. Students now learn an unfamiliar repository, propose a change, and explain their patch to open-source maintainers who might merge it. Eric opened up which lessons survived contact with his team's real work.
items.title: Stanford's CS146S teaches AI-native engineering with open-source maintainers reviewing student patches

items.summary: Three technical analysts weigh in on the Nifty ahead of Monday's session. Chandan Taparia of Motilal Oswal notes higher highs and lows over seven sessions and sees a rally toward 25,350–25,600 if the index holds above resistance at 24,444–24,600; he recommends a bull call spread for the November 23, 2026 expiry. Dharmesh Shah of ICICI Securities says Nifty broke an eight-month falling trendline and revised its target to 25,500, though overbought momentum may allow brief consolidation near support at 24,300. Nilesh Jain of Centrum Finverse points to a seven-session winning streak above 25,000 with caution warranted after India VIX surged nearly 14% to 17.58.
items.title: Analysts See Nifty Climbing Toward 25,600 on Bullish Technicals

items.summary: PM Modi, celebrating Diwali at Karanpur camp in Bastar on Sunday, said the end of armed Maoist insurgency did not mean the threat had vanished. He alleged that what he called 'Dimagi Naxals' had infiltrated political parties and organisations and were inciting people against the Constitution and democracy. Citing development milestones - more than 15,000km of roads built in affected areas along with over 9,500 mobile towers - Modi credited his government's strategy since 2014 for defeating Left-Wing Extremism.
items.title: Modi warns 'Dimagi Naxals' still inciting people after Maoist victory

items.summary: Donald Trump said on Sunday he was only kidding when offering UFC chief executive Dana White the job of White House press secretary. Speaking to reporters, Trump explained his joke and added that White liked the idea and is capable. The role has been vacant for three weeks since Katie Zacharia resigned.
items.title: Trump Retracts Joke About UFC's Dana White as Press Secretary

items.summary: The debt advice charity StepChange urges people to plan their Christmas finances now, saying it is never too soon. Its chief executive Vikki Brownridge warned the season puts pressure on household budgets and can cause January financial blues. It recommends budgeting in full, spreading costs, booking trains early, setting spending limits and checking cupboards before shopping.
items.title: StepChange Offers Christmas Money-Saving Tips Before Holiday Spending Begins

items.summary: Brent crude fell 64 cents, or 0.64%, to $97.67 a barrel by 1134 GMT, while WTI dropped 35 cents, or 0.40%, to $90.51 a barrel. Brent briefly dipped over $1 a barrel as traders weighed US-Iran tensions. Trump told CNN in a phone interview that fresh attacks were 'highly unlikely' unless Iran signs no strong agreement, though he had hinted at renewed strikes after last week's midterm elections.
items.title: Oil Prices Drop as Trump Downplays Iran Attack Risk

items.summary: Russia says it has recorded roughly 400,000 deaths of its citizens in the war on Ukraine since the full-scale invasion nearly five years ago. The figure comes from confidential data held by Rosstat, drawn from more than 11 million death certificates with details such as residence and age. About 392,700 certificates between Feb. 24, 2022, and late August 2026 explicitly link the deaths to the war via coding or text mentioning terms like “military operation,” “shelling” or “drones.” The data was obtained by Cyber Partisans and Silent Crow before being shared with a small group of news outlets.
items.title: Hacked Records Show Russia Recorded About 400,000 War Deaths

items.summary: Delhi's air quality index reached severe levels after the Diwali festival, with readings peaking at 406 in early Monday morning according to Central Pollution Control Board data. The city recorded an average AQI of 376 for the day, classified as very poor by CAQM. Around 20 of 59 monitoring stations fell into the severe category on Diwali night. Thick smog reduced visibility across several neighborhoods while PM2.5 remained the dominant pollutant despite firecracker restrictions. Experts attribute worsening conditions to unfavorable weather, vehicle emissions, celebrations and stubble burning. Delhi Minister Kapil Mishra accused AAP's Arvind Kejriwal of orchestrating a political campaign against Diwali under pollution concerns.
items.title: Delhi Air Quality Hits Severe Levels After Diwali Firecrackers

items.summary: Finshots explains that China is subsidising purchases of smartphones, electric cars and other goods through a national trade-in programme to boost domestic demand. The government set aside 250 billion yuan this year; last year it spent 300 billion yuan on the programme since 2024, which helped drive retail sales up by 0.6% to 2.6 trillion yuan and generated cumulative sales of 3.92 trillion yuan including 2024. The push follows pandemic lockdowns, property-sector debt limits and Evergrande Group’s collapse, leaving household consumption at around 40% of GDP. Finshots argues discounts only create a temporary pull-forward effect, so the real cure lies in strengthening China’s social safety net rather than relying on shopping subsidies.
items.title: China’s Trade-In Subsidies Buy Time Amid Deep Economic Weakness

items.summary: President Donald Trump announced on Truth Social that 'Task Force Iron Gate' is in full force against Iran, claiming the effort plus a naval blockade has choked off nearly all Iranian trade. CENTCOM established the Tampa-based task force under Admiral Brad Cooper to disrupt weapons and sanctioned materials movement across land borders and the Caspian Sea, while an existing July blockade targets Gulf ports. The announcement coincides with IRGC Aerospace Force claims of expanded domestic defence production.
items.title: Trump Announces Task Force Iron Gate Against Iran Trade Routes

items.summary: The Aramco Tower in central Riyadh was hit by an air attack on Saturday, confirmed via the Houthi-controlled Saba news agency. The Saudi energy ministry said it suffered only minor damage with no casualties, while BBC Verify footage showed more extensive damage to at least one floor. The strikes were part of renewed Houthi attacks against deep targets in Saudi Arabia amid intensifying conflict following an unravelled ceasefire.
items.title: Houthi Strikes Hit Aramco Tower in Riyadh

items.summary: Oil prices opened lower on Monday, with Brent crude briefly shedding more than $1 a barrel. US President Donald Trump said fresh American strikes on Iran were “highly unlikely” if negotiations made progress. Brent futures fell 52 cents to $97.80 a barrel, while WTI slipped to $90.68. Reports of shipping being hit near the Strait of Hormuz kept disruption concerns alive after over eight months of supply interruptions.
items.title: Brent Crude Falls as Trump Rules Out Fresh Iran Strikes

items.summary: Bowling coach Sitanshu Kotak confirmed that Arshdeep Singh, Gurnoor Brar and Auqib Nabi would remain with the team after the ODI series to prepare for the upcoming red-ball challenge against New Zealand. India lead the five-match series 2-0 following a DLS victory in Wellington. The squad is scheduled to begin its Test camp on November 11, which Kotak expects will help get them ready before heading to Hamilton for the third ODI.
items.title: India pacers stay back for New Zealand Test camp

items.summary: On Monday morning, the day after Diwali, Delhi's air quality remained 'very poor' with an average AQI of 376 at 7 am according to CPCB data cited by Hindustan Times. Several areas recorded readings above 400 in the 'severe' category, including Sonia Vihar (449), Burari Crossing (445) and Vivek Vihar (441). Firecracker emissions added to deteriorating air quality as transport sector pollution accounted for 19% of particulate matter. The Supreme Court had permitted certified green firecrackers only during limited windows, warning a complete ban would resume from November 9.
items.title: Delhi Air Quality Deteriorates After Diwali Firecrackers

items.summary: Political scientist Gilles Verniers discusses rising street protests by India's Opposition ahead of state polls in early 2027, framing them as part of a global democratic backlash. He notes the November 1 Delhi rally showed unity across parties but warns slogans like 'vote chori' risk voter disaffection if they delegitimize elections outright. Verniers argues institutional decay—especially loss of independence in the judiciary and Election Commission—is unprecedented since pre-2014, giving Opposition claims more weight than before. He outlines two conditions for protests to win votes: broad delegitimization of the ruling party and strong opposition organization, both still lacking. While acknowledging BJP's dominance and booth-level strength, he sees social media eroding its monopoly over information. The interview, conducted by The Federal with CERI researcher Verniers, positions these movements within worldwide youth-led revolts challenging illiberalism.
items.title: Verniers on India's Protests and Institutional Trust

items.summary: Vicky Kaushal and Katrina Kaif shared the first photograph revealing their son Vihaan's face on social media during Diwali. The image shows all three in coordinated yellow and cream traditional outfits, with the baby smiling and waving. This came a day after Vihaan celebrated his first birthday on November 7. Fans responded warmly to the festive post.
items.title: Bollywood Couple Shares First Photo of Their Son for Diwali

items.summary: European officials will attend this week's U.S.-mediated peace talks between Russia and Ukraine in the United Arab Emirates, France's foreign minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Sunday, days after Moscow insisted Europe had no role. The Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov earlier ruled out a European part, while President Trump suggested an agreement might involve all of Europe. Zelenskyy warned he lacked details and called the situation dangerous, likening it to Yalta in 1945. This is the fourth round since February's Geneva talks; Moscow returned only after envoy Steve Witkoff met Putin in October. Russia has demanded Ukraine cede territory and renounce NATO membership.
items.title: Europe Joins U.S.-Brokered Ukraine Talks in Abu Dhabi

items.summary: A large demonstration in Amsterdam, part of the Netherlands' ongoing "Red Line" protest movement, closed traffic streets around the Van Gogh Museum. Protesters waved Palestinian flags and chanted for action from The Hague, demanding tougher sanctions on Israel, a halt to arms sales, and recognition of Gaza as genocide. Organisers called these demands amid continuing tensions between the two countries over the humanitarian situation.
items.title: Amsterdam Streets Fill with Red as Gaza Protesters March Amid Israel Tensions

items.summary: India has safely evacuated 19 seafarers stranded for two weeks in the Yemeni cities of Hodeidah and Sana'a. The Indian Embassy said all were safe, in good health, and returning home via a post on X thanking those who helped facilitate it. India had earlier confirmed that 14 Indian nationals aboard a yacht off the coast were also safe; however, it remains unclear whether they are among the evacuated seafarers. The evacuation comes amid renewed Saudi–Houthi tensions threatening Red Sea shipping routes.
items.title: India Evacuates Seafarers Stranded in Yemen Amid Red Sea Tensions

items.summary: The Economic Offences Wing has registered a case after real estate developer Surendra Kumar Sampatraj Surana, owner of Surana Construction Pvt Ltd, filed a complaint about the redevelopment of Shivaji Nagar Co-operative Housing Society in Chembur. He alleges misappropriation of approximately Rs14 crore involving Mijit Ventures Pvt Ltd and Trust Capital, which he says disbursed only Rs19.50 crore against an Rs30 crore agreement while charging Rs38 lakh in fees. The complaint is under investigation.
items.title: EOW Opens Probe Into Alleged Rs14 Crore Fraud in Chembur Redevelopment

items.summary: In an FPJ exclusive, Drishyam actress Ishita Dutta describes her simple family celebrations of lights, rangoli and puja. She recalls lighting up the house with her father in Jamshedpur and shaping nariyal ka ladoos she still hopes to make for her children. On crackers, she says she has not burst any in about 15 or 20 years, advising people to reduce them over pollution.
items.title: Drishyam Star Ishita Dutta Recalls Diwali Traditions

items.summary: US, Russian and Ukrainian officials are expected to meet this week in Abu Dhabi for the first direct negotiations in nine months on ending the nearly five-year war. The talks will cover security guarantees for Ukraine, Europe's post-war security architecture and economic opportunities to support its reconstruction, according to envoy Steve Witkoff. Experts cautioned that a major breakthrough is unlikely.
items.title: US, Russia and Ukraine Set for Talks in Abu Dhabi

items.summary: At least three people died during Diwali celebrations across several Indian cities, with fires breaking out in shops, homes and commercial buildings. The deaths included a child struck by a rocket firecracker in Delhi's Narela area, plus separate fatalities from a Mumbai high-rise blaze and a Rajasthan shop fire that left two dead and three missing. Pune alone reported 63 incidents attributed to firecrackers, while other cities saw fires at showrooms, government quarters and residential buildings. Officials confirmed no injuries in some locations but awaited details elsewhere; one owner alleged arson after losing an estimated Rs 20-25 lakh.
items.title: Firecracker Accidents and Blazes Kill at Least Three Across India on Diwali

items.summary: A Red Line demonstration filled Amsterdam streets, closing roads near the Van Gogh Museum as crowds waved Palestinian flags and carried placards demanding an end to what organisers called genocide. Organisers urged tougher sanctions on Israel and recognition of its actions in Gaza. The event comes amid ongoing Dutch-Israeli tensions over humanitarian conditions there.
items.title: Amsterdam hosts large Gaza protest amid Israel tensions

items.summary: Residents and visitors returned on Sunday to the site of a Saturday 7 November attack in Kraków, where bullet marks remained visible on café windows. People examined damaged glass and lit candles at a makeshift memorial for six victims killed when a 24-year-old gunman opened fire in the historic centre.
items.title: Kraków residents return to scene of November shooting as memorial lights candles

items.summary: Millions across India celebrate Diwali, the Hindu festival of lights marking the triumph of light over darkness. The three-day festival features prayers, family gatherings and fireworks, but celebrations coincide with growing air pollution concerns in northern India. Delhi recorded its most polluted Diwali in a decade due to crop residue burning and firecrackers.
items.title: Diwali Celebrations Across India Amid Air Pollution Concerns

items.summary: Two hacker groups, Cyberpartisans BY and Silent Crow, say they breached Russia's Federal State Statistics Service (Rosstat) and calculated Russian losses in the war against Ukraine. Their tally ranges from 393,000 to 450,000 killed, with Kiberpartizany BY citing at least 393,881 as of 27 August 2026 and Silent Crow a higher figure of 450,100. The groups attribute the gap to different counting methods: one counts deaths caused by military action or its consequences; the other adds non-combat losses among personnel, terrorist-act deaths, and people registered in Russia who died in occupied territories or Ukraine where cause was unclear.
items.title: Hacker groups claim Rosstat breach yields Russian death tolls

items.summary: At a joint news conference in Shusha marking the sixth anniversary of Azerbaijan's liberation of Karabakh, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan reaffirmed Türkiye's support for Azerbaijan's efforts to establish lasting peace in the South Caucasus. Speaking with Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev present, Erdogan said the victory had opened a new era and called on both nations to turn battlefield success into stability. He praised reconstruction projects, including a 40-classroom school under construction in Aghdam covering 14,500 square meters, and cited joint initiatives such as an international forestry training center. Aliyev thanked Türkiye for its support during the war and described the two countries' unity as unshakable. The leaders also referenced the Shusha Declaration of June 15, 2021, which they said elevated their bilateral relations to alliance status.
items.title: Erdogan and Aliyev Reaffirm Türkiye-Azerbaijan Unity at Karabakh Anniversary

items.summary: An economic assessment by economist Stephen Kinsella, prepared for Fine Gael's A Blueprint for a Unified Island, estimates the first-year cost of Irish reunification at between €3 billion and €25 billion. The coalition partner published it on 08 November 2026. It examines four models—unitary state, federal system, managed integration and a higher-cost option—and notes that none would repay transition borrowing within 25 years under a 2% growth rate.
items.title: Fine Gael study projects United Ireland could cost up to €25 billion a year

items.summary: An article from Urdunama explains Allama Iqbal's concept of Khudi, noting it is often translated as the self but means deeper development through discipline and spiritual growth. On his birth anniversary, also World Urdu Day, selected verses revisit this philosophy of inner transformation and personal agency amid modern technology.
items.title: Khudi as Self-Development in Iqbal's Philosophy

items.summary: Assam Chief Secretary Ravi Kota chaired a monthly review meeting on Sunday, covering deregulation and business reforms, financial management, development priorities and administrative changes. He stressed time-bound completion of pending reforms by December 31, 2026, and noted a seven per cent reduction in e-Office pendency, with 3,04,288 files remaining. Kota urged departments to ensure coordinated action and accountability toward improved public service delivery. The article was generated from an automated news agency feed without text modifications.
items.title: Assam Chief Secretary Reviews Governance Reforms in Monthly Meeting

items.summary: CleanTechnica reports that Fortescue is installing wind turbines with blades measuring 89 metres at the Nullagine Wind Farm in Western Australia’s Pilbara. The company frames these as part of its real zero by 2030 vision, where turbine power will recharge electric dump trucks via 6MW robotic fast charging. CEO Dino Otranto said the green metal pilot is a significant milestone toward commercial-scale production from Pilbara ore. Fortescue describes plans for solar farms and battery storage connected by transmission lines to form an off-grid city-scale power system. The report notes these are Fortescue’s own statements, not independently verified claims.
items.title: Fortescue Unveils Giant Wind Turbines for Pilbara Green Grid

items.summary: NVIDIA and South Korea's Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT) are expanding their collaboration across the country's sovereign AI ecosystem, covering semiconductors, data center infrastructure, talent, startups, models, agents and security. The partnership lays groundwork for Korean NPU and XPU companies to join NVIDIA's NVLink Fusion ecosystem through training programs, hackathons and seminars. Through Korea's AI for All initiative, NVIDIA will work with three consortia and four foundation model builders using Dynamo software. It also announced a collaboration with SK Telecom and Rebellions, supported by MSIT, to advance sovereign AI infrastructure.
items.title: NVIDIA and Korea Expand Sovereign AI Collaboration

items.summary: Nvidia shares fell in out-of-hours trading on Nov 9, down about 3.4% to around US$180.30 from the Nov 6 Nasdaq close of US$186.64, after an internal investigation into whether chief executive Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort put his future under scrutiny. The probe followed reports that Huang had a relationship with Alice Huang, whom US authorities investigated as a Chinese intelligence asset. Nvidia AI Day Seoul will proceed; analysts warn of possible delays but expect limited impact on products.
items.title: Nvidia Shares Fall as Probe Into Jensen Huang Intensifies

items.summary: NVIDIA is helping advance Korea’s physical AI ecosystem by working with Samsung Electronics, Kakao Mobility and LG Electronics across semiconductor engineering, autonomous driving and robot learning. The companies apply accelerated computing, AI physics and simulation to move technology from development into real-world production. Samsung reported a roughly 1,600x speedup in one homogenization case, cutting simulation time from about 18 hours on a 32-core CPU to 41 seconds with GPU acceleration. Kakao Mobility plans a level 4 autonomous driving system around Kia vehicles, while LG demonstrated GR00T-powered robotic tasks using its CLOiD robot.
items.title: NVIDIA Partners With Korean Firms on Physical AI

items.summary: Samsung Electronics is preparing for a possible trial operation at its Taylor, Texas facility as early as mid-to-late December, ahead of mass production planned in 2027. The company has installed equipment and runs performance checks but has not confirmed the exact date, according to reports by The Korea Herald citing industry sources. Samsung remains second-largest globally behind TSMC's 72.5 per cent share versus its 5.9 per cent.
items.title: Samsung's Texas chip plant approaches December trial run

items.summary: South Korea's Vice Minister of Science and ICT Ryu Jemyung said on Monday (Nov 9) that contracted deliveries of Nvidia GPUs would proceed without disruption despite a controversy involving chief executive Jensen Huang. He told a parliamentary budget committee that 10,000 units funded under a 2025 supplementary budget had already arrived and were in use, with 2026 volumes expected to enter service this year. The ministry said it was monitoring developments while discussing prices and schedules with Nvidia Korea. Several events tied to Huang's daughter Madison Huang were cancelled, though Kakao Mobility confirmed its business agreement would proceed with senior director Gaurav Agarwal attending instead.
items.title: South Korea Vows Nvidia GPU Deliveries Will Continue

items.summary: According to a report by The Korea Herald, Samsung Electronics is preparing trial operations at its new chip facility in Taylor, Texas, as early as December. Preparations include installing equipment and recruiting engineers. A spokesperson confirmed the timeline last October. Mass production of 2-nanometre AI chips for Tesla is planned for 2027 under a USD 16.5 billion agreement.
items.title: Samsung's Texas Chip Plant Begins Trial Operations Ahead of Tesla AI Chips

items.summary: Jensen Huang, co-founder and boss of AI chipmaker Nvidia, is at the centre of a scandal after reports that he had an affair with Alice Huang, whom US intelligence believes was recruited by China to spy. The New York Times reported that surveillance revealed communications between her and Huang, who was identified through unmasking. Nvidia's board announced a probe on Sunday but said it has confidence in his leadership; sources say removal is unlikely given the money at stake. Trump, with whom Huang has a close relationship, said he had not spoken to him since news emerged.
items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang Faces Board Probe Over Alleged Affair With Suspected Chinese Spy

items.summary: A proposed Australian internet law, the Digital Duty of Care legislation, could require Google to block users under 18 from its Gmail service. An Australia-based company policy head said at a Senate hearing that an age-check provision risks overreach into private communications. The bill has passed the House but still needs cross-party support in the Senate and carries fines up to A$109 million ($75. 1 million). Meta, TikTok and Snap voiced similar concerns about regulators' broad discretion. Google's YouTube policy head Rachel Lord warned of potentially intrusive monitoring within messaging, email and private file storage.
items.title: Google Warns Australian Internet Safety Bill Could Block Under-18s From Gmail

The inquiry follows reporting that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort; Nvidia stated the Board has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised but would examine all available information. Singapore authorities reportedly questioned Alice Huang in 2025, and Trump was briefed roughly a year ago but took no action. There is no public evidence that trade secrets or national security data were compromised.

Nvidia became the world's most valuable company in June 2025 with a market capitalisation Forbes reported at more than $US5 trillion ($7 trillion). Trump said he had not spoken about the matter but would take Huang on his Asia trip, and Republicans have called for him to brief Congress.
items.title: Nvidia Investigates CEO Jensen Huang Over Alleged Chinese Spy Affair

items.summary: Sherry Zhu, a New York-based Chinese American creator behind the viral trend 'Becoming Chinese,' is travelling to Mount Siguniang in southwest China's Sichuan Province. Her content introduced young audiences to Chinese lifestyle habits and wellness traditions, inspiring renewed interest in Chinese culture. She now seeks to explore its scenery, Tibetan culture, and local way of life beyond the screen.
items.title: Creator Sherry Zhu Travels to Sichuan After Viral Trend

items.summary: Apple Pay's expansion into India may be entering a new phase, following its September launch with Axis Bank. Reports indicate HSBC India is reportedly in discussions to join the platform by year-end, which could offer credit card customers another contactless payment option using Apple devices. This follows an earlier indication from HSBC's mobile banking app listing showing Apple Wallet support.
items.title: Apple Pay Expands in India as HSBC Joins Talks

items.summary: Philip Strahan and Tuo Yang argue that unconventional monetary policy, including holding rates at the zero-lower bound and quantitative easing, shifted deposits toward more interest-sensitive customers. They conclude that this made deposit retention costlier and riskier for banks.
items.title: Unconventional Monetary Policy Made Bank Deposits Harder to Keep

items.summary: Hanna, Breza, Olken, Banerjee, Chandrasekhar and Moore report fieldwork in 600 Indonesian villages with over 5,500 villagers. They find that targeting consumption misses 77% of households with the highest marginal social valuation; self-assessed welfare targeting misses 57%; community ranking by level misses 25%. A randomized trial shows proxy means tests best target consumption, self-targeting ordeals capture self-assessed welfare levels, and community targeting comes closest to marginal social valuation. The authors note that targeting strategies inescapably embed normative stances.
items.title: Five Economists Question How Poor-Family Aid Gets Targeted

items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly warned senior Trump administration officials months ago that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had close ties to Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman suspected of working for China's intelligence agency. The claims prompted Nvidia to launch an independent investigation into the allegations.
items.title: Rubio Warned Trump Officials of Nvidia Chief's Alleged Beijing Ties; Company Launches Probe

items.title: Protesters Target Elon Musk's Austin Home After Midterms

items.summary: Researchers at MIT, the University of British Columbia (UBC), and elsewhere have developed WorldParticle, a deep-learning system that simulates many physical phenomena with one architecture. Unlike traditional tools hand-coded for each process, it represents materials as particles and learns governing dynamics rather than relying on programmed equations, allowing adaptation to unseen conditions. The team demonstrated higher accuracy across six scenarios, modeling protein structures about 100 times faster than numerical methods. Co-authors Peter Yichen Chen and Minghao Guo describe the goal of a foundation model for simulation that works out of the box.
items.title: MIT and UBC Researchers Build Unified AI Simulation Model

items.summary: MIT and New York University researchers present FLEX, an AI-assisted learning pipeline for robot motion-planning to be shown at the Conference on Robot Learning. The system lets a person guide a robotic arm using conversational language while the robot infers unstated preferences through three steps—Add, Generalize, and Mask—which together run in about five seconds. A large language model supplies common sense so that commands like “Don’t spill on the laptop!” lead the robot to avoid all electronics without explicit instruction. Study author Nathan Dennler notes LLMs absorb internet text into their reasoning; Andreea Bobu, who led the work, says FLEX lets a robot pick up what matters from just a sentence or two.
items.title: MIT engineers build platform helping robots infer intent from human commands

items.summary: Hindustan Times' morning brief of November 9 covers two top stories. Delhi's air quality was rated 'very poor', with the average AQI at 376 and several areas above the 400 mark, per CPCB data from Sameer app at 7 am after Diwali firecrackers. Separately, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang acknowledged an affair with a woman suspected by the US of being a Chinese spy, first reported by The NYT on November 7.
items.title: Delhi Air Quality Deteriorates After Diwali; Nvidia CEO Admits Affair

items.summary: Global oil prices held steady on Nov 9 after US President Donald Trump downplayed the likelihood of new strikes on Iran, though attacks near the Strait of Hormuz kept supply concerns alive. Brent rose to US$98.35 a barrel and WTI to US$91.30 by mid-afternoon Singapore time. Analysts warned geopolitical risks remained elevated while markets priced de-escalation optimism ahead of any Washington–Tehran agreement.
items.title: Oil Steadies as Trump Signals Restraint on Iran Amid Hormuz Risks

items.summary: Jensen Huang, Nvidia's founder and CEO, apologized Sunday to his family, colleagues and shareholders after admitting infidelity in an email stating there was 'no excuse' for his behavior. He acknowledged failing as a leader while reaffirming commitment to the company. Separately, The New York Times reported that Secretary of State Marco Rubio oversaw a classified memo warning officials Huang had ties to an alleged Chinese intelligence operative linked to Alice Huang at Megaspeed International.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Apologizes for Infidelity Amid National Security Probe

items.summary: Reports that Nvidia founder-CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a Chinese honeytrap operation have triggered an independent investigation announced by the company’s board on Sunday. The fallout may be unusually severe given Nvidia’s national security significance, its role in AI growth, and Huang’s centrality to it. Huang admitted infidelity but said he remained fully committed to the company. Analysts forecast sales could reach $1 trillion in 2029. Investors have urged support for Huang; hedge fund manager Bill Ackman was among them. The board faces questions about its earlier investigation and possible shareholder litigation, though an ousting looks unlikely given Nvidia’s strategic importance and lack of an obvious successor.
items.title: Nvidia’s board launches probe into Jensen Huang amid infidelity reports

items.summary: President Donald Trump publicly defended Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, saying he believes Huang should keep his job and calling him 'a fine person.' Trump said he had not discussed the matter with Huang. As an independent board investigation began into reports that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort, Trump acknowledged uncertainty but expressed hope everything was fine.
items.title: Trump Defends Nvidia's Jensen Huang Over Alleged Chinese Spy Link

items.summary: Senior Minister Lee Hsien Loong delivered the 2026 ABC Boyer Lecture, arguing that Australia and Asian nations must unite amid intensifying great power rivalry. Drawing on a century of Australian engagement in Southeast Asia and the Pacific, he highlighted historical security ties through arrangements like FPDA and Exercise Pitch Black, extensive economic links with China as its largest trading partner, and people-to-people connections via the Colombo Plan, which brought thousands of students to Australia from the 1950s onwards. He noted that resilience now requires partnerships rather than self-sufficiency alone.
items.title: Lee Hsien Loong Calls for Australia and Asia Unity Amid Global Uncertainty

Speaking to reporters, Trump called Huang an "honourable guy" who had done an amazing job for the country. Nvidia's board launched an independent investigation into allegations that Huang was targeted by foreign intelligence; the company said there is no indication national security interests were compromised and confirmed Huang agreed to cooperate.
items.title: Trump Defends Nvidia CEO Amid Chinese Spy Allegations

items.summary: Co-authored by Madiha Abid Ali and Yu Hongyu for CGTN, the article profiles Pakistani brand Hemani Herbals as it engages Chinese buyers at the 9th China International Import Expo in Shanghai. The piece frames CIIE as a platform built to open China's market rather than compete within it, citing the company's 2,500 products and presence in more than 85 countries. It notes Pakistan's exports to China reached $2.386 billion in the first eight months of 2026, a 40.51% year-on-year surge per China General Administration of Customs data, and points to ongoing free-trade negotiations as drivers behind the growth.
items.title: Pakistani Brand Hemani Herbals Expands at China Import Expo

items.summary: As China prepares to host the APEC Leaders' Meeting, most member economies are also represented at this year's China International Import Expo. At the food and agricultural products exhibition area, CGTN's Cao Chufeng spoke with companies from three APEC economies about how food innovation is crossing borders and how China contributes to this two-way exchange.
items.title: CGTN Explores Food Innovation Linking China and APEC Markets

items.summary: On Sunday, Nvidia said its board of directors opened an independent investigation after reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. An internal panel with outside legal advisers will oversee the inquiry.
items.title: Nvidia Board Launches Probe Into Jensen Huang's Foreign Ties

items.summary: Ehecatl Lazaro, a China specialist at the Mexican Center for Economic and Social Studies, told CGTN that Communist Party of China organizational discipline has underpinned its governance since founding in 1921. He contrasted this with Mexico's Institutional Revolutionary Party, which ruled from 1929 to 2000 before losing power amid weak internal discipline.
items.title: Mexican researcher credits CPC discipline for lasting governance

items.summary: BJP Union minister Giriraj Singh launched an attack on Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge for describing Diwali as 'khushiyon ka Eid'. Singh accused him of appeasement politics and dividing Hindus while pandering to Muslims, calling his true colours exposed. BJP spokespersons Gaurav Bhatia and Tuhin Sinha also criticized the remark over the weekend.
items.title: BJP's Giriraj Singh attacks Kharge over Diwali-Eid remark

items.summary: Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has formally requested a new passport and national identity card through lawyers at London-based Matrix Chambers, per Reuters. The request follows the reported cancellation of her existing documents by Bangladesh's interim government. It signals steps toward her planned December return from India after being ousted in 2024.
items.title: Exiled Bangladesh Leader Seeks New Documents Before Planned Return

items.summary: The abrupt failure of Ueno Bank left millions of Paraguayans unable to access their funds, triggering protests and the impeachment of President Santiago Peña on Friday. Authorities reported that nearly 1.2 million customers had received advance payments under the state deposit guarantee fund by Saturday, though many remained waiting. The collapse exposed a power struggle within the ruling Colorado Party after senators aligned with tobacco magnate Horacio Cartes withdrew political protection for Peña. Prosecutors charged him with breach of trust and placed him in pretrial detention; he pleaded not guilty. Vice President Pedro Alliana was sworn in to finish his term until August 2028.
items.title: Paraguay's President Removed After Bank Collapse

items.summary: Tandridge District Council is offering household grants of up to £250 to support residents with the cost of living. Applicants must live in Tandridge, be over 16 years old and prove financial hardship by submitting bank statements for August, September and October. Households without children can apply for £150; those with under 18s may claim £250. The scheme is worth a total of £150,000, processed first come, first served, with applications closing on 31 December at the latest.
items.title: Tandridge District Council cost of living grants open for Surrey residents

items.summary: A BBC investigation reports that drug gangs in Marseille are recruiting children into increasingly violent criminal roles beyond selling drugs. The reporting centres on DZ Mafia, which the head of France's anti-drug trafficking unit, Dimitri Zoulas, says became prominent in 2023 for using social media to market itself as a brand and released video statements denying involvement after one statement prompted police protection for a mayor. Two teenagers held by a gang sent a note saying they were being held captive; six men have since been sentenced over their treatment. Zoulas states France's drugs market generates €7bn (£5.9bn) annually involving 200,000 people and that cocaine users are expected to reach two million soon, up from 600,000 in 2017. During 2025 more than 10,000 children were involved in drug activity according to official figures. Gang members interviewed describe recruitment through promises of money and goods; one gang member implicated in murders says he climbed the ranks using his determination. Police say since 2024 about 1,000 individuals linked to DZ Mafia have been arrested, with 600 incarcerated.
items.title: French Drug Gangs Recruit Children for Kidnapping, Torture and Murder

items.summary: Paul Nowak, general secretary of the Trades Union Congress, warned ministers must greatly increase investment in youth employment support and avoid arbitrary benefit cuts ahead of Alan Milburn’s review. He called it a once-in-a-generation chance to secure young people’s futures while protecting the economy. A government spokesperson said £2.5bn has been pledged for youth employment support, delivering nearly 500,000 opportunities and up to 200,000 jobs through business engagement, with further reform following the review published in autumn.
items.title: TUC Boss Warns UK Needs Far More Youth Job Investment

items.summary: Murray Watt, Australia's environment minister, urged cabinet colleagues to stop undermining treasurer Jim Chalmers amid budget struggles and talk of cutting clean energy subsidies. Watt accused the Coalition of blocking $10 billion in savings.
items.title: Environment Minister Urges Labor Unity Over Treasurer

items.summary:
Two authors of a Mongabay-India commentary argue that India's drought early warning system reached some Rajasthan farmers in 2026 but failed others. The article notes IMD put the probability of El Niño developing during the monsoon season at 92%, and describes how connected farmers used advisories to stagger sowing or switch crops, while disconnected farmers waited on rain and lost harvests. It attributes quality problems to forecast precision limits and digital delivery blurring official messages with private ones, and notes patchy coverage and non-regional language reach isolated farmers late. The authors recommend coordinating agencies, targeting audio outreach through KVKs, rebuilding trust via direct contact, and adding weather stations. They state the research findings are yet to be formally published. Figures include a 21% shortfall in Rajasthan rainfall by early September and kharif sowing lagging about 16% nationally on July 10 at 53.12 million hectares against 63.27 million a year earlier.

items.summary: A G7 foreign ministers gathering in Paris on Monday offers the first chance for Washington's allies to gauge whether a midterm defeat for President Donald Trump changes U.S. policy toward Ukraine, the Middle East and its closest partners, four G7 diplomats said. Secretary of State Marco Rubio will make his first appearance before allies since the elections.
items.title: G7 Allies to Assess Trump's Midterm Setback at Paris Talks

items.summary: The Guardian introduces a podcast examining whether turning Europe's busiest shopping street into a traffic-free zone could rescue the popular but disliked and polluted thoroughfare. On Monday 26 October, the road was closed to vehicles as part of an experiment in pedestrianisation. Hosted by Dan Hancox and read by Troy Glasgow, the episode explores hopes that people will begin spending time there.
items.title: Guardian podcast asks whether pedestrianising Oxford Street can revive it

items.summary: Sai Life Sciences shares jumped roughly 9% Friday and rallied about 19% in three days after its July-September FY27 quarter. The company reported net profit of Rs 98 crore, up 17%, with revenue from operations rising 23% YoY to Rs Rs 659 crore and EBITDA climbing 20% to Rs 187 crore. Jefferies kept its ‘Buy’ call but raised the target price to Rs 2,050 apiece from Rs 1,610 apiece.
items.title: Jefferies raises Sai Life Sciences target price after strong Q2 results

Jefferies raised its target price to Rs 12,550 per share while retaining a ‘Buy’ rating; Nuvama cited an outperformance beat and maintained a Buy at Rs 12,000. Elara Capital noted revenue, EBITDA and profit exceeded estimates by 12%, 30% and 34%, but flagged uncertainty over whether elevated margins could be sustained across the full year.
items.title: Divi’s Laboratories Shares Rise After Q2 Profit Jump; Jefferies Raises Target Price

items.summary: Tasmanian Premier Jeremy Rockliff has confirmed that he and all parliamentarians are now receiving the full 22 per cent pay rise recommended by the Tasmanian Industrial Commission after a seven-year freeze. He had earlier said it was "out of step with community expectations" and accepted only a 3 per cent increase for himself, but Labor rejected a motion to disallow the rise in September last year. Rockliff now earns $369,000 a year, almost $68,000 more than before. The move draws criticism from health unions, which say nurses are offered rises of 3 per cent, 2.75 per cent and 2.5 per cent over three years while Treasurer Eric Abetz took a 22.36 per cent rise.
items.title: Tasmanian Premier Accepts Full Pay Rise After Initially Rejecting It

items.summary: The UN COP31 climate summit opened on 9 November in Antalya, Türkiye, running until 20 November and culminating in a consensus-based package of decisions. Talks centre on electrification with a '35-by-35' target, the transition away from fossil fuels, methane reduction through the Global Methane Pledge, and climate finance for loss and damage. A UNEP report published days before the summit found that even tripling current international public adaptation finance would meet just 23-29 per cent of developing countries' needs, leaving a shortfall central to negotiations. Türkiye's Environment Minister Murat Kurum said 'We will not look away, and we will not lower our ambition.' A People's Climate Summit is running alongside the talks from 9 November with more than 1,000 people signed up.
items.title: Climate negotiators open COP31 talks in Antalya

items.summary: The women’s singles final of the Chennai Open, between Janice Tjen and Magda Linette, was postponed to Monday after rain and thick smog from Diwali fireworks disrupted play. Organisers initially set a 9 pm start; the match never began due to low visibility. A post by coach Chris Bint alleged organisers wanted it to proceed despite bad air. The Women’s Tennis Association cited “unforeseen weather conditions.” Tjen, defending champion, criticised organisers online. Overall Chennai AQI was 138 on Sunday per Sameer/CPCB data; a separate monitor showed 1,556 at the venue though its source was unclear.
items.title: Chennai Open Tennis Final Postponed Amid Poor Air Quality

items.summary: On November 9, Paul Ford shared a Nudibranch-themed Faberge Egg he built in Three.js and asked Claude Opus 5.5 Medium to port it to Vanilla JS plus WebGL. The result came back at 98KB versus the original 77KB but was not identical. He noted that although he finds the Three.js version slightly easier to read, he rarely inspects such code anyway, while concluding that Claude Opus 5.5 can model in plain JavaScript and WebGL without Three.js.
items.title: Paul Ford Tests Claude Opus Porting a Three.js Egg

items.summary: On Sunday, world leaders including Emmanuel Macron, Anthony Albanese, and Mark Carney sent Diwali greetings to festival observers. Albanese called the celebration a symbol of unity across religious boundaries, while Macron wished people peace, hope, and unity. In Thailand, Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul inaugurated the 27-day Amazing Thailand Grand Diwali Festival in Bangkok, billed as the longest such event outside India. Other leaders from Sri Lanka, Pakistan, Israel, Malaysia, and the Seychelles also shared messages stressing compassion, prosperity, and harmony. The festival's themes of light over darkness resonated across nations celebrating on Sunday 2026.
items.title: World Leaders Send Diwali Greetings Emphasizing Unity and Peace

An example quote states: "It's very easy to spot an AI-written PR." They cite several datasette pull requests as examples and note that GitHub supports these tags natively in Markdown.
items.title: Author hides AI-written PR descriptions behind details/summary tags

items.summary: New data from Deel, a global hiring and payroll platform, shows India has the second-widest gap between maternity and paternity leave among 12 major economies. While typical Indian mothers take about 130 working days of parental leave, fathers usually take only seven — the shortest paternal leave in any country studied. The analysis covered close to 5,000 parents across Australia, Canada, France, Germany, India, Italy, Singapore, Spain, Sweden, the Netherlands, the UK and the US.
items.title: India Has Second-Widest Maternity-to-Paternity Leave Gap in Major Economies

items.summary: Civil rights activist Anand Teltumbde argues that the Modi government increasingly uses courts to suppress dissent when it cannot stop movements in the streets. He points to cases like the 2018 Bhima Koregaon incarceration of 16 activists and actions against those challenging the Citizenship Amendment Act. During October protests over Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, Delhi Police detained CJP leaders aboard an Air India flight after they posted Rs.50,000 bonds on October 10, and arrested others for trespassing at Jantar Mantar following its withdrawal as a protest site. Teltumbde contends these measures burden protesters without convictions while courts defer to procedural labels.
items.title: Indian Activist Analyzes Government Lawfare Against Protests

items.summary: Police said a notorious criminal named Deepak, 35, who was handling the operations of the Ashok Rathi gang after its founder was murdered almost six years ago, was shot dead inside his car on a service lane of the Delhi-Jaipur Expressway near Sidhrawali in Bilaspur on Sunday night. Investigators said the incident occurred between 11. 30pm and 11. 45pm but came to light around 8am Monday when commuters spotted the body, and that at least 15 rounds were fired, possibly from two sides.
items.title: Police Shoot Dead Deepak, Leader of Ashok Rathi Gang

items.summary: President Donald Trump told CBS News on Sunday that his mass deportation of allegedly undocumented immigrants was “too tough.” His party lost control of both Houses in the November 3 midterms, falling from a Senate majority to 44 seats and losing its House lead. Rising living costs, tariffs and the war with Iran also hurt approval ratings. Trump said he would work with Democrats on legal status for some migrants.
items.title: Trump calls his deportation policy too tough amid midterm losses

In Dwarka Sector 8, PM 2.5 levels exceeded 1500 while several government air quality stations stopped transmitting data during peak hours.
items.title: Diwali Cracker Bans Broken as Delhi Air Quality Soars

items.summary: Severe air pollution hit Chennai on Diwali, with thick smog and poor air quality despite cracker restrictions. An off-duty special sub-inspector died after a clash with youths bursting firecrackers in Tamil Nadu; three arrests have been made. items.title: Chennai Air Pollution on Diwali Despite Cracker Restrictions

items.summary: The BJP sharply criticised Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge for describing Diwali as a 'khushiyon ka Eid' and dared him and Rahul Gandhi to call Eid the 'Diwali of joy.' BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari said the party treated even festivals through vote-bank politics, while Gaurav Bhatia questioned why Congress would rename Hindu festivals. Tuhin Sinha accused the party of wanting to celebrate every festival as an Eid.
items.title: BJP challenges Kharge over Diwali remark

items.summary: The Thane district administration in Maharashtra banned sky rockets and aerial firecrackers after officials said 11 fire incidents occurred on Sunday, damaging public and private property. The order was issued by District Collector Shrikrishna Panchal Monday and took immediate effect until midnight January 8, 2027. Fires were blamed on falling residues igniting buildings; conventional crackers remain under existing laws.
items.title: Thane Bans Sky Rockets After Diwali Fire Incidents

Locals noticed the animal roaming and alerted others, then immediately informed Forest Department officials and urged them to take necessary steps to capture the leopard and prevent any untoward incidents. items.title: Leopard Sighting Triggers Panic In Medak Village

items.title: Oil Prices Fall as Trump Signals No New Attacks on Iran

items.title: Indian banks shut in ten cities for Diwali and Govardhan Puja

items.summary: In his first address as pope, delivered Sunday in Buenos Aires before President Javier Milei at the Palacio Libertad, Pope Leo XIV urged political leaders to reject corruption, heal polarization, and place the economy at the service of people. He warned that organized crime and corruption damage social coexistence and erode citizens' trust in institutions.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV Calls for Unity and Integrity in Argentina

items.summary: A detection service called Pangram found that many op-eds opposing the autonomous taxi company Waymo were written with substantial artificial intelligence input but carried no disclosure labels. The pieces appeared in outlets including the Dallas Morning News, San Francisco Chronicle and New York Daily News, registering between 68% and 95% AI-written on Pangram’s scale. Separately, The Washington Post reported that an anti-Waymo coalition spent more than $2.6 million on DC-area ads in 2026.
